tools.name: send

tools.description: WRITE, off unless the user put "send" in mcp.allow. Pastes a follow-up prompt (up to 20000 characters) into the window of a running task, as if the user typed it, and presses Enter. To a working agent the message goes into the agent's own queue. "Delivered" is said only on exact proof (the hook of the agent or its session transcript holds exactly this message); the answer is otherwise "w kolejce agenta – niepotwierdzone" (the screen shows it queued, nothing confirms it) or "nie dostarczono – tekst w polu wpisywania" (the paste stands in the input field). agentctl presses Enter only in the call that pastes, never later by itself. In the last case enter_only: true (no text) presses Enter for that text. It needs its own permission, send_enter, in mcp.allow. The first call (no confirm) only previews: it returns the exact text of the field, the screen state and a token for those bytes; show the text to the user, then call again with confirm: true and that token. It refuses (an error, no key) when the field is not byte for byte what agentctl pasted and what the preview showed, or a dialog is open. The answer keeps "Enter sent" apart from "delivery confirmed". An agent with an open question gets nothing pasted. withdraw: "<id>" (no text; peek lists prompt_queue with ids) takes back a waiting message: a queued one is removed, one whose delivery already began is marked stale instead (the agent may already work on it). With "agentctl watch" running, a send (also withdraw, and enter_only with confirm) is checked here without any lock, recorded and answered at once ("Accepted: send …"); the watcher delivers it at its next tick and events_since says the outcome (MCP WYKONANE with the delivery result, or MCP BŁĄD with the reason).
